text:
Sam H: heads-up — after the v3.2.0 runtime canary we pushed yesterday, SRE dashboard shows p99 jump for small-chat endpoints (models/rr-small-*). p99 went from ~220ms -> ~420ms across canary hosts.
Priya R: noticed the alert this morning. can you paste the query?
Sam H: `sum(rate(request_duration_ms_bucket{route=~"/v1/chat.*small",env=~"prod|canary"}[5m])) by (le)` — tail shows extra mass in 300-800ms buckets on canary.
Miguel C: any config changes in the kernel selector or batching? I rolled the selector patch that prefers 'sparse-attn-compat' kernels for those models.
Sam H: yes that patch landed in the runtime binary rolled to canary at 2024-11-02T22:14:32Z (deploy-bot note below).
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: runtime:v3.2.0 -> hosts: canary-*/poolB at 2024-11-02T22:14:32Z
Jen L: customers reported some slow API responses too?
Sam H: support ticket #65412 — small chat customers (short prompts) saw p99 spikes and a couple of timeouts. Not widespread but enough for an escalation.
Priya R: can you bisect by reverting the kernel-selector feature flag on one canary host? Miguel, can you toggle?
Miguel C: toggling flag on canary-3 now. Watch metrics..
Sam H: updated: canary-3 flag off -> p99 dropped from 430ms -> 230ms on canary-3 within 90s. Other canaries still high.
Miguel C: rolling the config change to canary-1 and canary-2 now (gradual).
Sam H: after rolling flag off across canaries, overall p99 back to baseline. Looks like the selector chooses a slower kernel for short-seq requests due to our cost heuristic.
Priya R: good repro. mitigation: revert selector default, keep optimized kernel rule behind opt-in, and add explicit length-aware heuristic.
Jen L: action items: 1) rollback selector default in v3.2.0 (runtime config toggle + ship emergency patch), 2) add a short-seq unit test that mimics small prompt profiles, 3) update canary playbook with quick bisect steps.
Sam H: also add metric: kernel_selection_latency{model,host,kernel} so we can trace which kernel path is chosen per request.
Miguel C: quick note — batching distribution changed slightly after selector; small requests sometimes got coalesced into a slow execution path. I'll add a sampling hook to capture batch composition for the next rollout.
deploy-bot: rollback started: runtime:v3.1.7 -> rolling to canary hosts at 2024-11-03T00:05:01Z
pagerduty-bot: incident ticket INC-2024-934 opened (priority: P2) — p99 regression on canary/runtime after selector change.
Priya R: communicate to support to pause customer escalations and inform affected customers we're rolling back and will follow up within 2 hours. Sam — can you prepare a short blurb?
Sam H: draft: "We saw an increased p99 on short-chat requests in our canary after a runtime kernel-selector change. We're rolling back the change and will validate with additional tests. No data loss. We'll follow up with root cause and mitigation timeline."
Jen L: +1. Postmortem owner? Priya wants to own RCA, Miguel will own repro + test, Sam will own rollback/monitoring changes.
Miguel C: follow-up: created a small repro harness that fires 1000 short-chat requests with t=token count distribution matching customers. script attached: 
```
for i in 1..1000; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{"model":"rr-small-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' &
done
```
Run with and without selector flag to compare p99.
Sam H: timeline update: rollback completed across canaries at 2024-11-03T00:28:15Z, p99 reverted. I'll keep the incident open for RCA until we have kernel-level traces.
Priya R: good. next steps: add canary gating rule that fails rollout if p95 or p99 increases by >15% within 30m for any short-seq route. Also add an automated bisect playbook snippet.
Jen L: I'll draft the gating rule and add to eng-release checklist.
Sam H: thanks all. I'll post follow-up once we have kernel traces and the test added.
Miguel C: FYI — learned that cost heuristic used model flops estimate + static batch threshold; need to feed empirical latency samples too. Will prototype.
Priya R: closing loop with support now.
Sam H: closing for now — marking incident as mitigated but RCA in progress.
